candidate.title: Collection des anciens alchimistes grecs, Première livraison (Pseudo-Démocrite, Physica et mystica)
candidate.ask_addressed: What textual and material evidence shows alchemy / early chemistry in Greco-Roman Egypt (Alexandria, Panopolis): Leiden papyrus X, Stockholm papyrus, Pseudo-Democritus Physika kai Mystika, Zosimus of Panopolis, Mary the Jewess (Maria Prophetissa) and her apparatus, Cleopatra the Alchemist? Dates, languages, and what they actually describe (practical dye/metal recipes versus theory).
candidate.quote: Les recettes mêmes sont comparables de tous points à celles du papyrus de Leide
candidate.summary: Berthelot prints Greek text and French translation of the Pseudo-Democritus Physica et mystica and says its gold and silver chapters are collections of practical recipes (surface-coloured metals, alloys) matching Leiden X, each ending with a 'nature rejoices in nature' refrain; he says the corpus has no magic in the recipes themselves, which separates the later mystical layer from the practical core.
candidate.limits: Berthelot's attribution of the school to Bolus of Mendes and a date near the end of the Ptolemies is his reconstruction. Lagercrantz (1913) gives no firm date. Not a modern critical edition.

candidate.quote: Cléopâtre, auteur de traités sur la distillation
candidate.summary: Berthelot says Zosimus' works already had the character of a compilation made about the 3rd century CE from Democritus and lost authors including Cleopatra (distillation treatises, with figures) and Marie la Juive (works on digestion apparatus and furnaces, with figures).
candidate.limits: The compilation dating (3rd century) is Berthelot's inference from manuscripts; Cleopatra is a pseudonym and the apparatus drawings survive only in medieval Byzantine manuscripts.

candidate.title: Collection des anciens alchimistes grecs, Première livraison (Introduction: origin of alchemy)
candidate.ask_addressed: Is there any evidence for alchemy in pharaonic Egypt before the Ptolemies? State what is absent as well as what is present.
candidate.quote: toute l'industrie des orfèvres et métallurgistes égyptiens qui a donné naissance à l'Alchimie
candidate.summary: Berthelot attributes alchemy's birth to the Egyptian goldsmiths' and metalworkers' industry. He bases it on the Greco-Roman papyri, so it is evidence for craft roots, not for a pharaonic-period text called or practising alchemy.
candidate.limits: Interpretive claim of 1887; he cites no pharaonic-period document in the passage read. It shows what proponents of an Egyptian craft origin rely on, and what is missing for an earlier date.

candidate.quote: Joignez le mâle et la femelle et vous trouverez ce qui est cherché
candidate.summary: Zosimus quotes Mary (Marie) repeatedly, on sulphur, copper-to-gold, the 'male and female' union and her apparatus. Her Greek works survive only through such quotations, so she is known at second hand from c. 300 CE onward.
candidate.limits: Her own date is unknown; Zosimus speaks of her as an earlier authority. A French translation by Berthelot, not the Greek read in context.
